documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, she's at home, baby napping.

Check-in. Consolidation going according to plan per heme/onc - arsenic cycles on and off, ATRA by mouth, counts holding up, ECGs before infusions fine per her. On leave from school this year, plans to go back in the fall. Tired some afternoons. No fevers, no bleeding. Thyroid meds and cabergoline unchanged, endo saw her in March. No seizures. Asthma fine.

Mood: some worry before each marrow/PCR check but sleeping and enjoying the baby. PHQ-9 3, GAD-7 4.

Plan: nothing to change from my side. Physical in the fall once consolidation is done. Message any time.

documents.title: Oncology letter
documents.author: hematology-oncology
documents.body:
Re: Morgan Sheehan - acute promyelocytic leukemia, t(15;17)

Dear Doctor,

Ms. Sheehan has completed consolidation with tretinoin and arsenic trioxide, last doses in late July. Peripheral blood PML-RARA PCR on 07/23/2024 is negative; she is in molecular remission. Both drugs are now stopped.

We will see her every 3 months with a CBC for surveillance. Please contact us with any unexplained bruising, bleeding, or fevers.

Hematology/Oncology

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual - after school, first week back teaching.

Year in review: postpartum PE 10/2023 (anticoagulation completed Jan). APL dx 11/2023, induction complicated by DIC, consolidation ATRA/arsenic finished July - PCR negative 7/23, molecular remission per onc letter. Surveillance with them every 3 months.

Now: energy most of the way back. Toddler on the move. No bruising, no fevers. Thyroid/pituitary followed by endo, no changes. No seizures. Asthma: albuterol a handful of times this summer.

Meds: phenytoin 300 daily, methimazole 10 daily, cabergoline 0.5 twice weekly, prenatal vitamin daily, albuterol prn.
Allergies: seasonal pollen.

Exam: vitals reviewed. Well-appearing, color good. Thyroid normal size. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no spleen tip. No bruising or petechiae. Calves soft.
PHQ-2 1.

A/P
- APL in remission: onc surveillance; CBC with diff today for our records.
- History of PE.
- Epilepsy: phenytoin level.
- Endocrine: endo.
- HM: flu and updated COVID today. Pap 2022 normal/HPV neg, next 2027.
RTC 1 yr.

documents.title: Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your blood counts are completely normal - hemoglobin back to 13. Chemistry and cholesterol normal, phenytoin 13.6. Good way to start the school year.

events.reason: Mouth ulcers, spreading blistering rash, red painful eyes

medications.drug_text: phenytoin sodium 100 MG Extended Release Oral Capsule

documents.title: Emergency Department Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
ED PROVIDER NOTE (abbreviated)

32F with epilepsy on phenytoin, pituitary macroadenoma, Graves, APL in remission (DIC during induction 2023). Three days of painful mouth sores and a rash that started on the trunk and has spread to the face, arms and legs; some areas blistered and broke open. Eyes red and painful.

Allergies: seasonal pollen. Meds per pt: phenytoin, methimazole, cabergoline, prenatal vitamin, albuterol prn.

T 38.9 C (102 F), BP 100/60, HR 110, RR 22.
Erythematous macules and atypical target lesions with dusky purpuric centers and blistering over trunk, face and extremities. Nikolsky positive. Hemorrhagic crusting of lips, oral erosions, bilateral conjunctival injection.

WBC 15.0, Hgb 13.2, Plt 250, ALT 45, AST 50, BUN 18, Cr 1.0.

Impression: Stevens-Johnson syndrome, phenytoin most likely culprit.
Plan: phenytoin stopped, added to allergies. IV fluids, analgesia, ophthalmology and dermatology called. Transfer to regional burn unit accepted.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily

documents.title: Burn Unit Discharge Summary
documents.author: burn surgery
documents.body:
Burn/Wound ICU - Brief Discharge Summary
Admit 01/06/2025 - Discharge 01/19/2025

Dx: Stevens-Johnson syndrome attributed to phenytoin.

Supportive care in the burn unit: wound care with non-adherent dressings, fluids, nutrition, pain control, daily ophthalmology lubrication and eye care, oral care. Her tachycardia on arrival settled as fever and fluid losses were controlled. Skin re-epithelializing well at discharge.

Neurology consulted for antiseizure therapy off phenytoin: levetiracetam 500 mg BID started. No seizures during the stay.

Discharge meds: levetiracetam 500 mg BID, methimazole 10 mg daily, cabergoline 0.5 mg twice weekly, prenatal vitamin, albuterol prn, emollients.
ALLERGY: PHENYTOIN - Stevens-Johnson syndrome. Avoid aromatic antiseizure drugs.

Follow-up: PCP 1-2 weeks; ophthalmology and dermatology as outpatient.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM after 2 weeks in the burn unit for SJS from phenytoin (ED 1/6, discharged 1/19). Summaries reviewed.

Skin is new and pink where it peeled, tender, using the emollients. Mouth healed enough to eat normally. Eyes comfortable with drops, has her outpatient eye appointment next week. Switched to levetiracetam by inpatient neurology - no seizures, a little tired on it, no mood change. Lost a little weight.

Meds reconciled: levetiracetam 500 BID, methimazole 10, cabergoline 0.5 twice weekly, prenatal vitamin, albuterol prn. Phenytoin OFF.
Allergies: phenytoin (SJS) - confirmed on our list in red. Seasonal pollen.

Exam: afebrile, vitals as charted. Skin: healing re-epithelialized areas trunk, arms, face, no open erosions, no signs of infection. Lips healed. Conjunctivae quiet. Lungs clear. Heart regular.

A/P
1. SJS - healing well. Keep eye/derm follow-up.
2. Epilepsy - on levetiracetam now. Seizure precautions reviewed; she can drive per neurology since no seizures.
3. Work - back to teaching 2/10; note sent.
4. Others unchanged.
See in 6 weeks.

Six-week check. Back at school since 2/10, tiring but good. Skin fully healed. Eye doctor released her. Mouth fine.

Levetiracetam: no seizures, the tiredness has worn off, no irritability. Neurology asked us to take over refills.

Onc surveillance in February normal per her. Endo stable.

Exam: vitals as charted. Skin healed, no blisters or erosions. Oral mucosa normal. Conjunctivae clear. Lungs clear. Heart regular.

A/P
- SJS: resolved. Phenytoin allergy on file; avoid related aromatic antiseizure drugs.
- Epilepsy: levetiracetam 500 BID, now prescribed here, 90-day supply.
- Rest per endo/onc.
Annual in the fall.

APL: remission, onc every 3 months, last visit August normal per her. Endo: cabergoline and methimazole unchanged. Epilepsy: seizure-free on levetiracetam. Asthma: albuterol in May/June, a few times a week at worst, otherwise rare. SJS healed.

Meds: levetiracetam 500 BID, methimazole 10 daily, cabergoline 0.5 twice weekly, prenatal vitamin, albuterol prn.

Exam: vitals reviewed. Well. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no organomegaly. Skin normal, no bruising.
